title: Systems Inquiry — IDEO Research Feature
description: A two-pane editorial spread modelled on design-research journals: a hairline-framed system diagram on the left, an italic pull-quote with em-dash attribution on the right. Distinguished by its single-family, three-weight type hierarchy and a tomato-red accent reserved solely for the diagram.
philosophy: This template exists for the kind of presentation that thinks before it performs. It treats the diagram as an intellectual equal to the written argument — not decoration, not filler — and gives both halves the same compositional weight. It refuses gradient fills, icon libraries, and any mark that cannot justify its presence. Built for researchers, strategists, and design practitioners who need to share process thinking with peers who will read carefully, not merely scan.
goodFor: Design-research readouts presented to cross-functional internal teams
3-line italic pull quotes with contributing researcher attribution
Conference talks for academic or practitioner audiences
Internal process retrospectives and methodology documentation
avoidFor: Sales pitches or investor decks requiring visual persuasion over analytical depth
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews with multiple data visualisation types
Brand launches or product reveals that depend on motion and spectacle
Audiences unfamiliar with systems-mapping or process-diagram conventions
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The title slide carries the quiet authority of a design-research journal cover — intellectually assured and stripped of ornament. Left pane evokes process and inquiry through a hairline-boxed diagram fragment with a single reserved accent; right pane gives the title room to breathe in a strict vertical hierarchy. The mood is deliberate and slow-reading, distributing compositional weight equally between diagram and text as intellectual equals. Avoid decorative fills, drop shadows, and any mark that performs spectacle rather than argument.

examples.layoutNotes: Two-pane split on a 12-column grid: left pane (cols 1–5) holds a hairline-bordered frame containing a spare structural element; right pane (cols 6–12) carries the title stack. Title in the heaviest weight positioned at the top-third of the right column, subtitle in lightest weight below, separated by a single thin rule; deck series or session label sits flush-left at the top of the right pane in the lightest weight. Generous 7% outer margin all sides; folio identity anchored bottom-right, no header band.

examples.promptCore: The slide holds the composed stillness of a peer-reviewed design journal — rigorous and unhurried, trusting the reader to spend time with both halves equally. Left diagram and right text exist in bilateral intellectual tension: neither illustrates nor decorates the other; both carry argument. The single accent color on the diagram should read like a scholar's annotation, purposeful and restrained, never ornamental. Avoid anything non-load-bearing: no drop shadows, no gradient fills, no flourishes that cannot defend their presence in the system.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">

examples.layoutNotes: The canvas splits into two near-equal columns divided by a single hairline rule — left pane at roughly 48% width houses the diagram inside its own hairline-bordered inset frame with the tomato-red accent used exclusively on nodes and directional connectors. The right pane, occupying the remaining 52%, vertically centers a three-line italic pull-quote in the mid weight of the type family, followed by an em-dash attribution line in the lightest weight, all set with generous vertical breathing room above and below. A 6–7% outer margin wraps the full spread; no header band interrupts the top edge. Page number sits flush bottom-right in the lightest weight, outside both panes.
